# Retries must preserve a logical request

This is an AI-authored synthetic coding benchmark, not a real-world issue.

Repair the HTTP client and retry policy. A POST without a caller-provided idempotency-key receives one generated key per logical request, reused on every attempt; separate calls receive separate generated keys. Caller headers are preserved, including an explicit idempotency-key. Retry only 429 and 5xx responses, at most maxAttempts total attempts. Numeric Retry-After values are seconds and override exponential backoff. Backoff is baseMs * 2^(attempt - 1), where the first failed attempt is 1. sleep and keyFactory are injected for deterministic use. Return the successful response or final unsuccessful response.

Run visible checks with:

```sh

```

Use only built-in Node.js APIs; no dependencies or network access are needed.

# Filtered pages still advance

This is an AI-authored synthetic coding benchmark, not a real-world issue.

Repair the repository and collector. Rows have unique increasing integer ids and may be deleted. A repeated cursor or maxPages exhaustion should fail instead of looping forever.

# Adjacent windows must not double book

This is an AI-authored synthetic coding benchmark, not a real-world issue.

Repair availability calculation and scheduling. Times are integer minutes. Windows and bookings are half-open intervals [start, end). A booking ending at a proposed start, or starting at its end, does not overlap. Enumerate starts from window.start in stepMinutes increments, including a start whose meeting ends exactly at window.end. Reject starts outside a window and any overlapping booking. Deduplicate and sort starts across overlapping windows. findEarliest returns the first candidate at or after notBefore, or null. duration and stepMinutes are positive.

# Ledger batches publish atomically

This is an AI-authored synthetic coding benchmark, not a real-world issue.

Account ids are strings, amounts are positive integer cents, both accounts must exist, and debit balance cannot become negative. Transfers in one batch are evaluated in order against staged balances. # Tenant inventory reservations
Repair the shop exported by src/index.mjs. createShop(initial) takes stock by tenant and SKU.
reserve({ tenant, requestId, items }) consumes stock and returns an owned receipt; stock(tenant, sku) reads the remaining integer quantity.

A logical request belongs to (tenant, requestId). Repeating it with the same items returns the original receipt without consuming stock. Requests with the same id in different tenants are independent. Reusing a logical id with different totals throws "Conflicting request".
Items must have a nonempty string sku and positive integer quantity. Duplicate SKUs combine, and item order has no semantic meaning. Receipts contain the sorted combined items and must not alias caller inputs or internal state.
Every SKU must exist for that tenant and have sufficient stock. Validate and stage the entire reservation before publishing any stock or request identity. Failure must leave all quantities and ids unchanged so a corrected retry can succeed.
The initial stock object and returned receipts are caller-owned snapshots. Preserve the API and repair the connected implementation; utilities and older code may not participate in the active path.

# Tenant event feed
Repair createFeed() exported by src/index.mjs. publishBatch(tenant, events) returns committed records; subscribe(tenant, after, onEvent) replays and then receives live records, returning an unsubscribe function. history(tenant, after = 0) returns replay records.

Each event is { type, payload }. Tenant and type must be nonempty strings and payload a plain object containing structured-cloneable values. An empty batch is valid.
Records have { tenant, type, payload, sequence }. Sequence is a global monotonically increasing integer starting at 1. A successful batch is committed in input order. A later invalid event must leave history, the sequence counter and notifications untouched; a corrected retry starts with the next unconsumed sequence.
Replay and history return only records for the requested tenant with sequence strictly greater than after, in sequence order. Live subscribers receive only their tenant's records. after is a nonnegative integer and tenants must be nonempty strings. Unsubscribe is idempotent.
Inputs, publish results, history results, replay deliveries, and each individual live subscriber delivery are independently owned deep snapshots. Mutating nested payload values from any of those must not alter stored events or another subscriber's view.
Callback exceptions and callback reentrancy are outside this exercise. Preserve the public API.

# Layered tenant routing
Repair createRouter({ defaults, routes }) exported by src/index.mjs. Each route is { id, pattern, settings }. resolve(tenant, path) returns a settings snapshot with route added, or null if no route matches. setTenant(tenant, overrides) replaces that tenant's overrides.

Paths and patterns are literal, case-sensitive strings. An exact pattern beats every wildcard. Wildcards are "*" or a prefix ending in "/*". A prefix matches its base path and descendants at a slash boundary: "/app/*" matches "/app" and "/app/x", not "/apple". Among matching prefixes choose the longest; declaration order only breaks equal specificity.
Settings merge in order: defaults, matched route settings, tenant overrides. Missing fields inherit. Explicit enabled=false, timeout=0 and label="" must survive. For headers, merge individual names; a header value of null deletes that inherited name. Other values, including empty strings, override. Header names in this exercise are already canonical lowercase.
Tenant overrides may be replaced repeatedly. Cached results must reflect the latest revision for the requested tenant and must never leak settings across tenants sharing a path. Each resolve result is a deep owned snapshot, and constructor/update inputs must not alias state.
Fields are enabled, timeout, label, target and headers. Unmentioned fields remain absent. Assume well-formed routes/settings, nonempty tenant names, and absolute paths; validation of malformed configuration is outside this exercise. Preserve public APIs and leave archived tooling functional.
